title: Ser715 Phosphorylation Induces beta-Hairpin Unfolding and Destabilization of FOXM1 Autoinhibition.
authors: AlRawashdeh, Sara; Obidat, Raghd; Del Moral-Morales, Aylin; Medina-Franco, Jose L; Velazquez-Martinez, Carlos A
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文通过5微秒全原子分子动力学模拟揭示FOXM1磷酸化诱导β-hairpin解折叠及自抑制解除的构象变化机制，核心聚焦蛋白质构象采样与结构动态计算，方法为MD模拟，与课题高度相关。
abstract: FOXM1 is a cell proliferation-driving transcription factor activated by phosphorylation-induced conformational changes. In its inactive state, an intramolecular beta-hairpin within the transactivation domain (TAD) binds the N-terminal repressor domain (NRD), forming a composite beta-sheet that locks the protein in an autoinhibited conformation. Despite the known importance of this regulatory switch, the molecular events that unlock FOXM1 remain poorly characterized. Here, we performed 5 mus all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of human FOXM1b NRD-TAD complexes in both unphosphorylated and tetra-phosphorylated states, modeling four experimentally validated regulatory phosphosites. Our results showed that phosphorylation induces local unfolding of the beta-hairpin beginning at Ser715, located at the hairpin turn, and propagates to global disruption of the NRD interface through hydrogen bond loss, salt bridge rupture, and secondary structure collapse. In contrast, the unphosphorylated complex maintains stable hairpin geometry and interdomain contacts. Additional replicate tetra-phosphorylated simulations and a monophosphorylated Ser715 simulation reproduced the beta-hairpin unfolding event, supporting both reproducibility and the sufficiency of Ser715 phosphorylation in initiating this transition. Per-residue MM-PBSA energy decomposition further reveals that phosphorylation redistributes interdomain interaction energetics, with Ser715 emerging as the dominant locus of energetic perturbation despite the presence of multiple phosphosites. Together, these findings support a phosphorylation-triggered order-to-disorder transition that relieves FOXM1 autoinhibition and highlight Ser715 as a key structural and energetic switch. Our study provides a dynamic molecular framework for targeting FOXM1 activation via its regulatory fold.
abstract_zh: FOXM1是一种由磷酸化诱导构象变化激活的细胞增殖驱动转录因子。在其非活性状态下，反式激活域（TAD）内的分子内β-发夹与N端抑制域（NRD）结合，形成复合β-折叠，将蛋白质锁定在自抑制构象中。尽管已知此调控开关的重要性，但解锁FOXM1的分子事件仍鲜有表征。在此，我们对人FOXM1b NRD-TAD复合物进行了5微秒全原子分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟，涵盖非磷酸化和四磷酸化状态，建模了四个经实验验证的调控磷酸化位点。结果表明，磷酸化诱导β-发夹从Ser715（位于发夹转角处）开始的局部解折叠，并通过氢键丢失、盐桥断裂和二级结构崩溃传播至NRD界面的全局破坏。相比之下，非磷酸化复合物保持稳定的发夹几何结构和域间接触。额外的重复四磷酸化模拟和单磷酸化Ser715模拟重现了β-发夹解折叠事件，支持了该转变的可重复性以及Ser715磷酸化在启动此过程中的充分性。逐残基MM-PBSA能量分解进一步揭示，磷酸化重新分配了域间相互作用能量，尽管存在多个磷酸化位点，Ser715仍成为能量扰动的主要位点。综合这些发现，支持了一种磷酸化触发的有序到无序转变，解除FOXM1自抑制，并突出Ser715作为关键结构和能量开关。我们的研究为通过其调控折叠靶向FOXM1激活提供了动态分子框架。
